Anesthesia was discontinued due to suspicion of malignant hyperthermia (MH).  2 h after terminating anesthesia, the patient developed tachycardia of (160 bpm) and max creatine kinase (CK) was 5800 U/l. Myoglobinuria was detected. Hours later, the patient presented muscle pain and weakness and general pain. Three individuals from the same family carried the T allele and in vitro contracture test (IVCT) was positive for MH susceptibility (MHS) for all three. The T allele is designated as MHS-causative by the European Malignant Hyperthermia Group.
Sentence: Allele T is associated with increased risk of Malignant Hyperthermia when exposed to succinylcholine as compared to allele C.

Notes: Case report. A female patient with breast cancer was treated with tamoxifen, 3-amino-1-hydroprolylildene bisphosphonate and 5-fluorouracil. She developed severe toxicity in 2 weeks of treatment, and 5-fluorouracil treatment was stopped. Toxicity was diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, leukopenia. Analysis of DPD cDNA showed heterozygosity for a 165bp deletion that results from exon skipping. Sequence analysis of the genomic region encompassing the skipped exon showed that the patient was heterozygous for a G to A point mutation in the invariant GT splice donor sequence in the intron downstream of the skipped exon. This variant is now referred to as DPYD*2A. DPD activity in leukocytes (3.1 nmol/mg/h) was decreased compared to mean activity of DPD in controls (9.6+/-3.7), and comparable to that observed for obligate heterozygotes.

Notes: This Y3933C variant is part of a 3 variant haplotype: RYR1 I571V (rs146429605);R3366H (rs137932199);Y3933C. The variants of the triplet, (p.Ile1571Val), (p.Arg3366His),(p.Tyr3933Cys), are of unknown significance, and contributionof  each  of  them  as  well  as  their  combined  effect  on  RyR1function has not yet been ascertained. The Y3933C variant is described as probably damaging in Polyphen and pathological in Pmut. A female index patient, aged 37, had presented with delayed motor milestones since the age of 3. Histological analysis confirmed the presence of fibrosis, and core-like myofibrallar alterations in muscle tissue (minicores and central cores). In vitro contracture testing (IVCT) confirmed a diagnosis of malignant hyperthermia susceptibility (MHS). Western blot analysis showed that the muscle contained 50% less RYR1 than control. The patient's father and sister were also diagnosed as MHS via IVCT, while her mother refused IVCT testing, and agreed to genetic testing. A triplet of RYR1 variants (571V;3366H;3933C) was found "in cis" in the index patient, her sister, and their mother. The father did not carry the triplet, but did carry a fourth mutation (c.14545G>A (p.Val4849Ile; rs118192168G>A), which the proband also carried in "trans" to the triplet. The authors conclude that the RYR1 "cis" triplet of variants contributes to the MHS phenotype, and the rs118192168G>A variant contributes to the central core disease phenotype.

Notes: Case report. A 63-year-old woman developed Lieberkuhnien adenocarcinoma. She was treated with FOLFOX regimen (includes fluorouracil, leucovorin and oxaliplatin). 8 days after the first infusion, she was hospitalized for grade IV stomatitis, as well as anal and vaginal mucosa erosions. She also had a fever and diarrhea with pancytopenia. Blood cultures were positive for E. coli and Enterobacter aerogenes. She was eventually transferred to the ICU for septic shock with multi-organ failure. Clinical examination showed necrotic mucositis to mouth, anus and vulva with diarrhea and defenseless painful abdomen. Lab tests showed bicytopenia (neutrophil count 0/mm3, platelet count 19,000/mm3), coagulopathy, metabolic acidosis, hyperlactatemia, hepatic cytolysis, renal failure. CT scan showed parietal pneumatosis of small intestine. The patient died three days after admission to ICU after she suddenly presented with intracranial hypertension related to a large intracranial hematoma. Dihydrouracil/uracil ratio was 0.1 (normal >6.0), indicating complete DPYD deficiency. DPYD genotypic investigation of 464T>A, *13, *2A and rs67376798 showed heterozygosity for *13 (rs55886062). However, the authors note that this mutation likely only explains part of the case severity, and that complete DPYD sequencing has been undertaken.

Notes: The rs118192172 T allele was reported in a German pedigree where the proband died of a fulminant malignant hyperthermia (MH) episode after exposure of halothane during general anesthesia. The sister of the proband inherited a TT genotype for each haplotype associated with the T allele. The mother, sister, and two sons of the proband had the T allele and the MHS phenotype. One daughter of the proband that carried the haplotype carrying the causative mutation, tested as MH negative (MHN) demonstrating possible discordance between phenotype and genotype. On the other branch of the pedigree, a father and his two sons did not carry either haplotype associated with the T allele and all three were diagnosed as MHS via IVCT. The T allele is designated as MHS causative by the European Malignant Hyperthermia Group.
Sentence: Genotype CT is associated with increased risk of Malignant Hyperthermia when exposed to halothane as compared to genotype CC.

Notes: "We found the following variants that might reduce the odds of ATDILI occurrence during the anti‐TB treatment: rs1367731, rs6913008, and rs9276975. Specifically, only 7 of the 385 identified cases of ATDILI exhibited a homozygous TT mutation in the rs1367731 locus, which was associated with a decreased risk of ATDILI under both the genotype and recessive models (OR = 0.43, 95% CI = 0.20–0.98, p = 0.039 and OR = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.18–0.93, p = 0.033, respectively, Table 4). Similar results were observed in SNP rs6913008, where TT genotype carriers were significantly less likely to develop ATDILI (TT vs. CC, OR = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.18–0.93, p = 0.027; TT vs. TC + CC, OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.17–0.89, p = 0.024, Table 4). Additionally, TB patients with the TT genotype in rs9276975 exhibited a marginally lower risk of ATDILI compared to those with TC or CC genotypes (TT vs. TC + CC, OR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.23–0.98, p = 0.045). However, it should be noted that all associations reported were not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Utilizing linkage disequilibrium (LD) information from the 1000 Genomes Project, the three SNPs exhibiting near‐significance had high LD with each other (r 2 = 0.90), thereby indicating that rs9276975, rs6913008, and rs1367731 could be considered as proxies for one another."
Sentence: Genotype TT is associated with decreased likelihood of Drug-induced liver injury when exposed to ethambutol and isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin in people with Tuberculosis as compared to genotypes CC + CT.
